dedupe_keys.name: hidden water geography of us hyperscale data centers cooling versus electricity water use 472 facilities

description: This preprint maps the two physically distinct pathways through which data centres consume water: on site for cooling, and in the power system that generates their electricity. The authors link the locations of 472 US hyperscale facilities to electricity regions, hydrologic basins and water-stress data. Under baseline assumptions operational water consumption totals about 300 gigalitres per year (range 205 to 451 across scenarios), with electricity-related water contributing three quarters. The pathways have different hotspots: direct cooling burdens concentrate in stressed western and south-central basins, while electricity-related burdens concentrate in a few eastern grid regions with fossil-heavy supply, and just 3 of 24 hosting balancing authorities account for 59 percent of electricity-related water. The paper concludes that cooling design and local water sourcing matter locally, and electricity planning and procurement matter regionally. Producer: Gianluca Guidi and a co-author, submitted to arXiv on 5 June 2026. Coverage: the United States. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv; the abstract page does not say whether the facility list is released. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: a preprint whose scenario ranges are wide, and results depend on published facility locations and water-intensity assumptions. Simulation uses: it is a method and benchmark for water-stress exposure of data centre siting and for coupling grid and water models. Related record: UK data centre water stress (data-thirsty-ai-uk-data-centres-water-stress).
